Diving back into a world of chaos with Kaiman and Nikaido. This is Dorohedoro once again. So, as a reminder what I'd thought about the previous season and the OVA before jumping into this. The first season was a near-masterpiece and the OVA was a chill episode with a collection of six-short bonus chapters from the manga. What does this season uphold? A lot going on with old and new characters that converge into one gnarly finale that's set up for the next season. Kaiman and Nikaido are traveling through the World of Sorcerers up until Mastema where theymeet a young woman named Natsuki, voiced by Sara Matsumoto (Japanese) and Anairis Quinones (English), who followed them because of Kaiman having Cross-Eye tattoos as she has one over one of her eyes.  She is willing to lead them to their hideout.  Meanwhile, we meet the Cross-Eyes gang that En thought he'd got rid of except there are only a few of them that Risu, voiced by Soungdok (Japanese) and Alejandro Saab (English), who lived within Kaiman's esophagus and now is revived thanks to Kikurage and know who really killed him.  Before I continue, I didn't mention this character because Risu does pop up after being revived.  It was technically a spoiler.  I'd also learned that in the English Dub, Billy Kametz voiced Risu before his unfortunate passing and Alejandro took over since 2022.  Rest in paradise, Billy.  Back on the topic of the Cross-Eyes, the remaining members consist of Dokuga, voiced by (Kouki Uchiyama (Japanese) and Kieran Regan (English), who can dress up like a moth, fly like one, and produce poisonous saliva; Ton, voiced by Katsuhito Nomura (Japanese) and Johnny Yong Bosch (English), who does knife tricks; Ushishimada, voiced by Atsushi Imaruoka (Japanese) and Christopher Swindle (English), who has super strength; Tetsujou, voiced by Daiki Kamano (Japanese) and Benjamin Diskin (English, who has lightning reflexes with a sword; and Saji, voiced by Tomokazu Koshimura (Japanese) and Bill Butts (English), who is the youngest of the group.  For the moment, the Cross-Eyes are making ends meet, living in this home owned by this landlady until they plan to usurp the En Family.
As speaking of the En Family, they also have a lot going on such as Chota disguising himself as Nikaido since a Devil named Asu has had her escape from En's supervision until the gig is up.  Chota also finds a secret journal about Nikaido that involved her childhood, including an adopted family and her magic being the mythical time manipulation magic.  In addition, we learn that one of Nikaido's adoptive family members is still alive.  During a dream sequence En offers, Ebisu remembers that she had a family and travels to where they are located.  Shin and Noi travel meet up with Kasukabe, Jonson, Vaux and Thirteen to find the location of the Cross-Eyes with the help of Kasukabe's estranged wife, Haru.  However, it's not so easy when the conflict becomes brutal and complicated, especially when it comes to their leader.  I've mentioned the past, and this anime does more than what it offers as we learn more about Kaiman's true identity.  Although, it is also complicated when Kaiman is suffering through major headaches as he remembers his past that is connected to Risu, who has a lot more on his plate, too.  Even more so when we make it to the finale when the tide of power turns between the Cross-Eyes and the En Family.  I won't spoil anymore than I've already shared because the story goes a mindfuck.
Yes.  It does sound like the story does go a little all over the place when we have multiple characters going out their way as well as we learn more about them.  However, that is the point.  We learn about these characters, especially Kaiman and Nokaido.  Keeping the themes of identity along with institutional trauma and the moral blur between factions.  What I'd forgotten to mention in my review of the last season is that there are no signature protagonists or antagonists.  Sure, we have a division of class between humans, sorcerers and devils socially and politically.  No matter where you stand, life sucks.  You will have your fair share of friends and enemies.  En may be a narcissist at times when he does care for his family, but the Cross-Eyes have their share of blood in their hands even if they usurp En.  I would also agree that you might hate Kaiman for what he'd transitioned to once he'd learned about his true identity.  So, despite the story for every character going all over, their stories do converge into what the next season might be when someone else takes over the throne.  As a matter of fact, the characters are still pretty good with their own goals and their chemistry with one another.  Finding out about some of the other characters aside from Kaiman and Nikaido like Professor Kasukabe and his wife, Haru, and Ebisu with her family are entertaining in terms of character exploration.
In the meantime, the animation itself continues to add the sort of mind numbing moments in the chaotic world of Dorohedoro.  The way the animation runs is much more improved when it comes to 3D modeled characters moving like 2D characters.  The character designs and the background are still amazing in terms of variety, exploring new places while retaining that dystopian charm.  It still has a butt load of gore and blood as the narrative goes.  The action is still as metal as it can be.  If I have to nitpick a little, it'll be when you see multiple healing factors come into play.  I know Dorohedoro takes place between the Hole, the World of Sorcerers and Hell, but it feels like the healing magic that is shown can be a bit of a copout at times.  But I digress.  It is Dorohedoro and like I've said in the last season, you throw your morals out of the window while retaining some emotion like empathy, rage, and delight.  The voice cast, including  the new ones, are still amazing when I've watched the show twice.  One in Japanese and one in English.
Overall, like in the last season, this season is near-perfect as it started off casually after walking away from a chaotic finale back into some more chaos up to an even more gritty abrupt finale that's set up to what the third season will continue where it'd left off.  Right after the conflict between one family to a faction they'd thought was gone.  With even more chaos along with new places to explore, Hell isn't too far off since the anime is pretty much located right around the borders between the World of Sorcerer's and Hell.  It's also interesting to know that Devil Exams have more than what it was in the last season.  I'll give this chaotic second season eight bandaged Kaimans out of ten.  8/10.  Yes, I know this is like a point lower than the first season.  It's why this season is more chaotic than the previous season has been.  Where would the third season bring us?  Find out more.  This is Dorohedoro.

entry.title: Futsutsuka na Akujo dewa Gozaimasu ga: Suuguu Chouso Torikae Den

results.review:
Though I Am an Inept Villainess is a charming, if ultimately overly simplistic take on the villainess subgenre. The narrative structure and general vibe of the character writing feels almost fairy tale-like, and while this does make for a vibrant and upbeat tone and compelling ensemble, a good deal of it feels a bit flat or lacking in depth, with the more outright antagonistic characters being too comically evil or mean-spirited in certain instances. The way that Reirin navigates being trapped inside the villainess’s body is generally very intriguing and did keep me interested in seeing how she would continue winning people over to herside, but the fact that this experience doesn’t really change her outlook or perspective on anything dulls a good chunk of my interest.
It is certainly a well-produced series on most fronts. Solid character designs are bolstered by rich color choices and the general competency and lack of jank you expect from a studio like Doga Kobo, and the timing of the comedic outbursts had me chuckling along more than I expected. I do wish that it had maybe reached for it a little harder though, as, despite its obvious polish, it also lacks anything particularly eye-grabbing. Overall, this is an exceptionally competent series, which is more than I can say about a lot of anime, but it’s also one that I’m probably going to forget about fairly quickly due to a distinct lack of substance both narratively and visually. The fact that I spent a good portion of my watch time thinking about how the actual villainess’s storyline was far more interesting certainly didn’t help, but I don't think I wasted my time either so I can still give it a decent recommendation.

entry.title: Clevatess II: Majuu no Ou to Itsuwari no Yuusha Denshou

results.review:
Long story short: This season was mediocre at best, if not bad. ----- Unfortunately, Clevatess 2nd season is one of those sequels that does not deliver the same of its prequel. 1st season was fleshed out, with a nice pacing and good development even for secondary characters. You could feel that excitement and anxiety of "what will happen next?", hoping everything will be 'daijobu' and that they will overcome that tough situation. Now, the second season simply does not deliver any of that..... ..
.
It decided to be uninteresting, mediocre and... school. Yes, you read that right "SCHOOL". Magic... is it the remake of Harry Potter already? I thought it would be released just in December this year. You start to wonder if it's the same anime you watching. 

Alicia does not shine as much. It's not Alicia's fault, it's just how mediocre the writing is. 

Every Alicia's "deaths" are basically ALL SAME. Every Alicia's struggle are basically same. This shows how lame and boring the writing is. 

You have random students that does not add nothing to the show. Nothing. And on top of that Nelluru has about 10 seconds of screen time the whole season. They add a bunch of random students but they put aside the most sweet and likeable character of the anime. 

The 2nd season drama is fully based on manipulation. Even a mirror or a piece of branch is ready and steady to manipulate or mind control the characters. Lame. Lame. Manipulation for the sake of plot device everywhere... everywhere. 

At its core, the story tries too hard to 'paper over the cracks'. By the final episodes, you can guess why the Dark Beast of the North is doing what he's doing. But you know when they try to make it seem complex just to make it falsely intriguing? When in the end the root of it all is stupidly simple.

For last: The flashbacks. Yes. Flashbacks are are hit or miss. But most of the times they'll be a miss. Flashbacks need that perfect timing; flashbacks can't spoil the mood nor interrupt the excitement, and they can't be much. Unfortunately, it's not what happens here. I would say there is at least 3 or 4 episodes of flashbacks that you could careless. 

I wish I could say something nice here, but unfortunately there isn't much. And I wish I could have enjoyed this season. Maybe I was harsh in this review exactly because I cared about the 1st season and so I was expecting the 2nd season to delivere same.


-------

If I could say something to my past self before watching this 2nd season, what would I say? 
"Watch this second season only if a 3rd season is announced and/or if you deeply care for one of the characters. Otherwise, don't even bother".

If a 3rd season ever happen, I'll watch it, but expecting it to be as good as the 1st season, otherwise I won't think twice before dropping =/

entry.title: Mushoku Tensei III: Isekai Ittara Honki Dasu

results.review:
I am so, so conflicted on how I feel about Jobless Reincarnation. It consistently scores well on MAL, but I'm consistently lower than most on it. I've had to somewhat adjust how I watch this series, and even though it has somewhat helped, it's really not what got me into the series to begin with. I'll assume you've seen the previous parts of Jobless Reincarnation for the purposes of this review. Story & Characters: Mushoku Tensei: Jobless Reincarnation Season 3 actually takes us to Eris and we basically get to see what she's been up to since we last saw her. It'sonly for the first two episodes, but is is probably the best episodes of the season - for better or worse is up to you.  You can tell she has gone through some growing pains, but really has one goal - seeing Rudeus after getting much, much stronger.  She ends up going to Gull Farion, known as the Sword God.  It's there that we get to see her grow, alongside of other trainees.  Not really a spoiler, but her ability to "play well" with others (or lack there of) is somewhat hilarious to watch.  She's aggressive, and extremely passionate about her goal and I love it.  She's a really strong character and these two episodes reinforces that.  You see her briefly at the end of the series, and it caps off her "arc" in a nice way.

The rest of the series revolves around Rudeus with, his now, two wives in Sylphiette and Roxy.  As individual characters, all three are strong.  They have this very firm belief that family is everything, and will do their best when they, or those close to them, need help.  And that's the biggest strength of this season: It's all about character building.  The show does such a good job at building up these characters and adding more bulk to their lives.  Rudeus has made such a strong, positive impression on those around him, that they can't help but follow him.  This includes Cliff, Zanoba and Nanahoshi.  When Rudeus and gang are off to their next quest, no matter how dangerous it might be, they all go together.

That being said, what got me into Jobless Reincarnation in the first place was about the adventure and the fights within them, both of those, for the most part, are kind of absent.  Now that Rudeus has found a home, the series' story mostly revolves about going from his home base and to the next destination.  Again, it's fine, but not what got me into the show to begin with.

Aside the Eris arc, Nanahoshi has a pretty sizable arc.  Rudeus and gang end up traveling and meeting some pretty significant people along the way.  The conclusion in episode 10 was awesome.  The biggest problem is that there's so much weird storytelling in the middle that feels like filler that I'm not sure how worth it ends up being.  Yes, it's all positive character building for minor characters, but it doesn't feel like it adds much to the macro-story of Jobless Reincarnation.

Perugius is introduced during the Nanahoshi arc, and I really was expecting him to be an old geezer with not much to say.  I was very, very wrong.  Boring as her may come off as being, he listens well and has some great things to say.  I was surprised that I liked him as much as I did.

What does add is the flashback in episode 13.  This is flashbacks done right.  It's aggressive, violent and really quite shocking.  I saw online that they actually did hold back based on what the original source material said in terms of the levels of violence that was initially shown, which is somewhat disappointing.  That being said, we get the idea of what they were going for, and more.  But this somewhat reinforces my point - this season as very obvious highpoints, but with too many low points in between.  (Story: 6/10, Characters: 8/10)

Art: Studio Bind has gone a pretty good job and giving this series a steady level of animation.  Previous seasons had bumps along the way, but based on what I saw, it looked a little more polished this time around.  (8/10)

Sound: I really like this series' approach to their opening theme, as it's a not always a pre-determined bunch of scenes, but rather, shows us part of the story instead.  It's got obvious cons, but is a net positive in my eyes.  Voice work remains strong here.  I love hearing Lindsay Seidel (Eris) back voicing, as I really haven't heard her in much these days.  This is probably Suzie Yeung (Nanahoshi) at her best, though I'm really not surprised at this point.  Bradley Gareth (Gull) and Kenny James (Perugius) apparently voiced in previous parts, but I don't recall them saying much - they were great here.  (9/10)

Overall: Mushoku Tensei: Jobless Reincarnation Season 3 had really solid high points, but I've obviously expressed my disappointment in others.  I'm 100% with you if you like this series because it tries to do its best to be right by its characters.  I get that.  And if you were to tell me that the series isn't about worldbuilding and action, then I'd obviously believe you.  I plan to watch it right until the end regardless, but if you *really* want to watch it for the season reasons I did, you might be lower on it than I am.  (8/10)

Magical Shopping Arcade Abenobashi is a true masterpiece of anime. I had no idea at all what this was one was about and put it on one weekend as some background filler while I did some drawing … I didn’t draw a thing I just sat there and took this excellent anime in for all it’s worth. There are other reviews telling you all about the characters and the settings and the plot - so I just want to tell you how this show made me feel. This show took me on a ride that I did not expect at all and I am grateful forit. The way it pokes fun at and parodies almost everything about anime is exactly the sort of thing I enjoy. Those who can step back and laugh at themselves and the things they love have a special power - and this show absolutely has that power locked down. 

 Anime fans will recognise tons and tons of references to other shows and genres - this entire show is paying respect to anime in general while also pointing a finger at how silly anime gets. I love this sort of thing - humour and action and hi-fiction all combined together to create something that just feels so damn good. This show was created in 2002 but it has that old school heart that older anime had - I can’t explain it in words - just some anime had a vibe that is almost unknown today - and when I find one of the shows that has that vibe I hold onto it dearly. I love to laugh - and Abenobashi makes me laugh a lot - like a LOT. 

 What really struck me about this show was how it goes from slap-stick madness and fan service to really emotional moments - and then back again. To be able to shift gears like that in a story like this takes something special and Abenobashi does it masterfully. The expressions in this show - the relentless savage critique of the genre - the way they handle the Pikachu knock off - it’s all solid gold. Pewy ?

 An extremely well done anime that I would recommend to any and all fans of anime - and for those of us who’ve been around a bit and seen more than our fair share of anime this one has a little something extra in the sauce. I will absolutely be coming back to watch this one again and again for many years to come.

+ Really, really well written and a gripping show, Characters are really capatavating and its themes are really original with the mixture of history blended into the animes story. Show also makes use of non-linear story telling in an original way! I mean watching the first episode just hooked me in, instantly. - Some of the episodes do feel like 'Filler' and the pacing mid-way in the show kinda sucks. I also thought a specific character escaped death too many times and some of the story telling aspects are left too 'ambitious' for my liking. Ending thoughts: Its really capturing and is pretty well written,but for the episode amount, Im unsure if its really equal in story telling aspects compared to the amount of time I was watching the show. It was incredibly enjoyable through its characters however, because theyre so unique. Whilst a part within the story is a bit vague (apparently its explained better in the novel) it is a really good show. I wouldnt reccomend it to a beginner watcher (because of the episode count) but someone whos into anime, 1000%.

entry.title: Kimetsu no Yaiba Movie 1: Mugenjou-hen - Akaza Sairai

results.review:
Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba Infinity Castle I is the first part of the three-part Demon Slayer movie coming. And finally, after a year, it was released on Crunchyroll. I'll assume you've seen the previous parts for the purposes of this review. Story & Characters: I don't think there's any secret of what Demon Slayer's about at this point. Tanjiro is on his quest to both find a way to return his sister, Nezuko, into a human, and to slay the head of all demons, Muzan. Now, Tanjiro and company enter his Infinity Castle, where he, all the Hashira and several othermembers of the Demon Slayer Corps. are stuck, duking it out with any demon that heads their way.  The three-part movie kind of comes down as a necessity, due to all the concurrent fights going on at the same time.  We'll tackle them one by one here.

Shinobu vs Upper Moon Two, Douma: This is a decently solid fight.  We really haven't seen Shinobu tasked with fighting a difficult foe yet, unlike many of the other Hashira, so seeing how she fights does feel pretty refreshing.  She fights differently than many other Demon Slayers, and you can tell her intelligence gives her the edge on most any foe.  Kanao makes an appearance late in the fight, and even though she doesn't really add much herself, her connection to Shinbou remains strong.  As per usual, we get to see some of the past of Douma, and even though the flashbacks are usually pretty intrusive to the pacing, I actually thought they kept it brief here.

Zenitsu vs Upper Moon Six, Kaigaku: Kaigaku replaced Daki and Gyuutarou after the Entertainment District as Upper Moon Six, which we saw briefly after the conclusion of one of the seasons.  Though we don't know much about him, his connection to Zenitsu becomes much more clearer, and I was also a fan of how this one panned out.  Like with Douma, they kept the flashback brief.  This is a very different story from the one prior and it remains flashy to watch... for obvious reasons.  This kind of resolves how I feel about Zenitsu as a character, even if he clearly is the "third" among the intimal trio.

Tanjiro and Giyuu vs Upper Moon Three, Akaza: Getting to see Tanjiro and Giyuu fight together is awesome to experience after all this time.  They made a conscience effort to remind us that Tanjiro is very clearly not at Giyuu's level in terms of fighting skill, and I like that.  Even though this is probably the best of the three fights, they really overcorrected with how much they think we would like Akaza's story.  Don't get me wrong, his past is *the* best out of any of the Upper or Lower Moon demons so far, but the pacing here is easily the worst.  We continually get stuck in a loop during the current time and while I get a lot of it is about his conflicted past, they overdid it.  The two main characters, along with the story, were really strong, but this could have been executed a little better.

Upon the conclusion of these three fights, our gang continues onto the castle, and, my assumption, is we'll see more of the Hashira in action.  We obviously have a lot more demons to go, and I can't wait to see it - whenever it airs.  (Story: 7/10, Characters: 9/10)

Art: The art and animation remain some of ufotable's top work - and that's a big compliment, coming from the same studio that produced other masterpieces like those in the Fate series.  (10/10)

Sound: The work of Yuki Kajiura is obvious, and her all in this series should be highly commended.  I've said it before, but Demon Slayer has attracted some of the top VO talent on earth, and the fact that every single Hashira is voiced by such a big name speaks volumes.  Channing Tatum joins the movie in a minor role - apparently his daughter's a big fan of the series, which is awesome.  Rebecca Wang also joins in a minor role, as is very strong here.  I'm a little surprised Kyle McCarley (Yushiro) and Laura Post (Tamayo) returned, as both have said their pieces against various works in the past.  I wouldn't be shocked if this was a union works, but perhaps it is, due to what the movie is.  (10/10)

Overall: Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba Infinity Castle I is the first of three parts of Demon Slayer movies and there's no doubt that it starts out very strong.  Top notch story telling remains a strong point, but the series just can't get away from its bad pacing.  This isn't to say it ruins the movie, but when the same criticism remains in every Demon Slayer part, you kind of expect it.  Still, the series is extremely strong, and I wouldn't dare miss the rest.  (9/10)

Don't get me wrong, I didn't put this as "mixed feelings" because I didn't enjoy it, but this is not really something that would be enjoyed by someone who enjoys more straight-forward stories. The premise is pretty strange, but hey! I'm all for strange stories! The animation was very good (although flashy at some times) and the ending was...somewhat confusing. It's understandable if you take some time to process it, but it was pretty quick and can feel like 30 bullets shot at you if you're not ready. (But it has been a while since I've watched it, so I might be incorrect!) I did findmyself a bit bored when they were playing that one game, but I can't speak for everyone.

Overall, it's a very cute and pretty deep story, but I wouldn't reccomend it for those who dislike fast-paced films.

I have never seen an anime so blatantly tell me to go fuck myself and that my time was wasted as I have with B the Beginning season 2. I loved B the Beginning season 1 and it is one of my favorites. B the Beginning Season 2 starts on a strong note for the first half of the first episode. Then they decided to regress Keith Flick as a character. Keith's journey in season 1 is learning to trust others and chasing a revenge that he ultimately forsakes in order to save the people that he loves. They tell him that he doesn't need to fightalone anymore. So season 2 starts with him walking into a trap, alone, and getting turned into a plot device. I think Episode 4, talking about how Keith fell in love with his step-sister was disgusting. I think that making that a plot point really took away from his character. His conversation with Erika and Gilbert weren't satisfying either. That's to say nothing of what the show does to Lily.

Lily was supposed to be just as capable and smart as Keith. So naturally, she spends the whole series playing Initial D and contributing nothing to the plot. But it gets better when you realize she was supposed to do something to help find Keith. But it doesn't matter, because the show can't even commit to its own plot or the story it wants to tell.

The group needs to search 4 towers to find Keith. They split up, with 4 people moving to cover 3 towers. Lily doesn't do anything. Yuna being treated like she needs to be carried is an insult to what we saw from her in season 1 too. I was okay with Izanami being back but that also amounts to pretty much nothing.

The show isn't confident to commit to anything. The series starts with Koku being held hostage with Keith being captured, and being threatened to comply or that Lily and Yuna would be next. Koku, instead, rebels against Kirisame and instead of killing Keith or following through on their threat, they do nothing. Then, suddenly, instead of needing Koku they can copy his abilities to a new Gen Jetblack or whatever the fuck they wanted to call that blonde girl. But then they don't even do that because Koku beats her in a poorly animated slow motion slog of a fight.

The King and his successor are irrelevant, but apparently Kirisame was playing a double agent. For why? Fuck if I know. We learned nothing about Kirisame. He showed up four times, two of which were just the bad guys (?) saying "it's just like you planned." What plan? Excuse me? We don't know his motives. At the start we are told that he wants to "rid the world of the reggies so that they can start a new world." By the end, we learn that this isn't true, because why else would he betray the successor and work for the king? Who is his posse and why do I care? And instead of explaining, the show ends on a fight between Kirisame and Koku where Kirisame says "you are ignorant of everything." Okay. Enlighten me. What am I missing?

This whole season feels like the outer frame of a puzzle with every interior piece missing. Outside of Keith Flick's character assassination, Lily's uselessness, or the random bs with Asagiri, I do believe that there was a framework here for an amazing followup to B the Beginning. Unfortunately, compressing it into 6 episodes and a complete and utter lack of direction or endgame leaves the entire season wasting every episode trying to find some new direction to propel itself before finally ending just when we might be getting started.

It's such a disappointment when the original series, while convoluted, was perfect and upon a rewatch can be enjoyed even better. This feels like how in the 90s they'd release amazing OVAs, only to follow them up with a full season, direct-to-VHS anime series that would completely miss the point of the original, except in reverse. I can't say I just want it to end here though. I feel like Production I.G. owes me a third season for wasting not only the time I spent on this season, but the time I spent waiting for it to come out, and the years I spent avoiding it because I was scared it wouldn't hold up to the original. Production I.G. needs to renew B the Beginning and try again with a full length season. Not some tie-in movie that shortens the original manga arc and misses the point.

Kill la Kill is a great example of what anime can be when you put some heart and soul into it. I’ve been watching anime since the 80’s and without question Kill la Kill is among the best of the best of the best. Yeah it can take a second to get past the raging fan service and the tiny tight outfits - but at the same time this entire show is taking those overused tropes and making them the story - and our hero isn’t some generic dude - it’s a girl out for revenge who is just as pissed off about thesilly outfits as all the haters. This show takes many of the tropes that anime haters hate on the most and rides them in for the win. 

 What seems like a cut and dry story wound up being way more than I expected. For a show as frantic and fast paced as this one it still manages to generate several moments that make you stop and think about what just happened and why. I wont drop any spoilers here so I’ll just say that most viewers will start this show on one side of a fence or the other - and by the end of it Kill la Kill does a great job of blowing that fence away entirely. 

To be honest I didn’t sit down to write a review for this show at all - I really just want to talk about Mako Mankanshoku. After re-watching this show for the third time I must proclaim Mako Mankanshoku as my all time favourite anime character , bar none. Her undying energy , her undying faith in her friends , her undying willingness to sacrifice herself , her undying love for her family , her undying belief in herself and her willingness to act selflessly from the beginning right through to the very end all qualify her as the goat. The way they animate her scenes of encouragement - the way she affects everyone in the story with her blazing positivity and her unwillingness to give up - I can’t really think of any other character that even comes close to being as amazing as Mako.  This show has an S level cast and for Mako to stick out among them is a true testament to the awesomeness of her character. 

 I strongly recommend this show to all fans of anime. Yes there’s an almost cringe level amount of groin snapping costume changes and underboob in this show but that’s actually part of the story and if you get it you get it - if you don’t then you won’t and that’s fine. The animation , the characters , the setting and even the way it all ends are excellent. I could really deep dive into this show but I see other reviewers has already taken care of that - so I shall wrap this up with the one thing that has stuck with me after watching this show for the 3rd time … 


Mako Mankanshoku forever.

entry.title: Kono Subarashii Sekai ni Bakuen wo!

results.review:
After watching every Konosuba anime adaptation, I saved this one for last, and it was worth it, both as a farewell until season 4 and as a timekiller, of sorts. Being basically what konosuba has been all the way, there were still some things that I've liked in here that were looked over in the main series, such as the whole deal with the Crimson Demon Village, who turned out to be way cooler folks than I thought, also some more screen time for Megumin's sister, Komekko. Knowing where it'll all lead made all encounters look much more exciting to me, seeing how Megumin's life completelychanged after meeting Kazuma, and it even ended up being a little tearjerking. Opening and Ending were very good, might I add.
I find it to be a fitting & enjoyable prequel that'll either sate your yearning for more Konosuba, or for more Megumin, or for both at times, though I recommend watching it only after you've watched everything else of Konosuba, so it can be more entertaining ( and also because it's not AS entertaining as the main series, so saving it for last would be better) That said, I ended up really liking Yunyun more...

I can’t express how awe struck I am with this show, everything from the writing, to the direction, both of art and the action sequences, to the MUSIC DIRECTION (arguably the best part) is just done so masterfully, with so much love, thought, efforts and care put into them Starting off with the overall setting and atmosphere, its so beautifully tragic, everything in night city represents the peak of how a hyper-capitalistic world and city would look like, with corporations fighting over tech/economic and social power to rule and expand their operations, no matter the cost borne, as long as it doesn’t overpower the profits, nothingmatters, Their cruel and clever nature are at the very epicenter of Night city and kick off the story as a whole, Everyone is selfish, everyone is cruel, trust is a valuable asset, sharing which with the wrong person may lead to destruction and death

Coming to the start of the story, Man is it great, David and his mother represent the common everyday family, they don’t have a lot of money or resources, yet they still work hard to keep things afloat, specifically David’s mom in this case, willing to give up everything if it means her son could have a better life than hers, Which only makes the events that succeed more impactful and tragic, we get to see glimpses of how this world treats those who don’t have a lot of monetary or social importance, both of which can only be gained in this world through exploitation, of people, or resources, of markets.

Moving onto the main characters, they’re so incredibly human despite being cyborgs, and that’s the greatest accolade I can bestow upon them, They may seem cruel on the surface, but that’s the bare minimum that is needed if they wish to survive in Night City, They represent camaraderie, fraternity, love and it’s really refreshing to see how in this city of mega capitalistic soul-less corporations, Our crew represents they few remaining individuals that are human, Maine (the initial leader of the crew) and his guidance to David, Rebecca and her brother and their sheer madness and loyalty, and Lucy and the romantic tension between her and David are just great to witness, these dynamics are what keep the story engaging, and are well developed enough to emotionally impact the viewer when something affects our crew, They represent us, they aren’t the mega rich, they are just trying to make a living at best, and everyday is a gamble,

From here I believe the most important and impactful elements of the show must be discussed, Ambition, Dreams, Family, and Life as whole, Lucy’s dream and how central it is to the plot is revealed much later on, though its omnipresence throughout and how it shapes the dynamics between her and David Is just so fascinating to witness. I won’t spoil much but I was just devastated by how melancholic the story becomes, yet still being so packed with action. the actions which David has to take, the emotional toll on him due to his actions, his brain and identity not being able to grasp the sheer volatility and pace through which his life is moving through, Him kind of becoming everything he hated, Him feeling alone, with each action being selfish and selfless at the same time, and at the end him partaking in something he knows for a fact he won’t be able to back down from due to all of this emotional burden and the way the story unfolds, all of this was something which explored beautifully in such a short span of time

The antagonists are so well written in every aspect of the definition of well written, they’re witty, cruel, apathetic, chasing only and only self satisfying profits, destroying everything and everyone who dares step in between, Especially Faraday, yet somehow their actions don’t feel without a purpose, it is exactly because their actions have a purpose and are so deplorable that the antagonists become so frightening.

The show does something wonderful and that is not speaking much and instead showing us, it’s evident everywhere from the characters’ faces to the destruction caused to the actions taken. The Show SHOWS more than it tells and when it does tell we all cry in unison, That’s how masterful writing is done

If you want clinical depression mixed with witnessing some of the best creative direction, music, storyline, a progression which flows like Butter where nothing feels rushed, paired with a story that is more expressive and emotionally impactful, all of this in 10 eps, just go for it, no second thoughts, Edge-runners does a lot of things in 10 eps which major shows can’t accomplish even a 100. It's the kind of masterpiece you don’t get to witness very often, Loved it<3

entry.title: Super no Ura de Yani Suu Futari

results.review:
Smoking Behind the Supermarket with You is an anime, particularly for those who are somewhat or well into their careers, that will feel relatable and leave you with a sense of hope. It gives perspective that even when things feel gloomy and the job, hours, or life suck, you can still find moments that brighten up the day. The little things still matter and make a difference, and you can find those moments anywhere. The story is slow-moving, has no major plot points or progression, and the characters are not that deep—but that is what makes it good and drives the message home. Sasaki is asalaryman who works a demanding job, leaving him to feel lonely because he doesn't have much time for his personal life. Tayama/Yamada is a young adult who works as a cashier at the supermarket Saskai goes to. Despite it not being the most interesting or fulfilling role, she still loves what she does. 

Together they break up the mundane parts of life and enjoy eachother's company and conversation over a cigarette. Over time, they develop a deep friendship (or perhaps more?) and help each other grow as they work through the tough moments of life. 

The artwork is also good and helps show the characters' emotions very well. This is a great watch if you're looking for a slice of life that you can actually see yourself in, or could see someone else in.

⚠ SPOILERS AHEAD ⚠ There is a lot of potential in Black Torch. And honestly, that's exactly what disappoints me the most about it. The Mononoke and their amazing character designs, paired with the premise, make this feel like it has all the makings of a really good action anime. The problem is that, after finishing the show, I feel like I've seen far more of what it could be than what it actually is ( ￣︿￣) And that brings me to my biggest issue with this series: THE COMBAT... or rather the lack of it! It's not even that I disliked one particular fight or that there werea few fights that didn't live up to the hype. It's that, time and time again, the show sets up a confrontation, makes it look like something exciting is about to happen, and then fails to deliver ANYTHING!

I don't need every single fight to be some masterpiece of animation. But I do need the anime to actually SHOW ME THE FIGHT! If a character is going to unleash an attack, then let me see the attack. If two characters are going to clash, then let me experience that clash instead of having the most interesting parts barely shown IF AT ALL.

And the opening theme makes this even more frustrating.

There are some genuinely cool visuals in that opening that made me wish the actual anime had done more with its characters. Take Koga, for example. There's a scene where he's walking toward the camera, his horn begins to manifest, and the horn pushes his hood back as he continues walking. It's such a simple thing, but it looks incredibly cool. It gives him a presence that makes you want to see more of him.

Except we don't get that scene in the actual show.

Then there's the part near the beginning where Jiro's frame overlaps with Rago's. Rago's eyes light up, and we see that shadowy, distorted version of his true form emerge. THAT is the kind of design I wanted to see!

And then we get to Rago's actual true form in the anime, which looks like a solid 3D-rendered object that someone dropped into the show!

I'm not even exaggerating when I say that it looks like someone came up with a rough concept for Rago's true form, rendered it in 3D, and then kept it in as the final design.

What's even more confusing is that the show itself gives us a reason to question this decision.

In episode 11, we see these giant flying bugs, and they look considerably better to me. Their teeth look better, their animation looks better, and they generally feel more convincing as giant creatures. So why does Rago's true form look so much worse?

We've had anime like Naruto animating enormous creatures for decades. This isn't some impossible challenge that nobody has figured out how to handle. And I could understand using CGI if Rago's true form were constantly moving around, fighting dynamically, and performing all kinds of complicated attacks. At least then, I'd understand what the production was trying to accomplish.

But what does Rago actually do?

He hops around a few times... that's it! why did they have to render that in 3D? LOL

That's pretty much what we've seen from him in terms of action so far. And for that, we get a design that looks so noticeably out of place!!

I just don't get it.

And after all of this, I was still hoping that the final confrontation would finally give me something worth getting excited about.

At the end of episode 11, Jiro and Amagi's clash begins, and it looks promising... then I remembered that there was only one episode left.

Even if the entirety of episode 12 were dedicated to their fight, which it wasn't... would that really be enough time to deliver the kind of epic clash this setup seemed to promise?!

NO! the fight was okay.

That's it. It was okay.

To give it credit, it's definitely the best fight in Black Torch. Compared to the other fights in this anime, it actually feels epic. But that's also a pretty low bar to clear when ALL of the previous fights have been disappointing. Put it next to the fights in other action anime, and I don't think it would be particularly impressive.

And that's the problem. Even when the show finally gives us its biggest confrontation, the one that should leave us with a strong impression of what this series can do, I still come away thinking about how much better it could have been.

However, there is one thing I genuinely liked about the ending, and that's Amagi himself.

When Jiro punches a hole through his chest, there's a subtle shift in Amagi's facial expression as he realizes that it's over for him. What I liked about this moment is that, despite everything, he stays true to his convictions until the very end.

Just moments earlier, Amagi had said he would destroy Jiro if he couldn't obtain Rago's power. Yet, even then, it never felt like he acted out of any personal hatred toward Jiro. Jiro was simply standing in the way of his goal, and Amagi was willing to eliminate him to achieve it. But when the moment finally comes and Amagi realizes he's lost, he accepts that his goal is no longer attainable rather than becoming petty and trying to take Jiro down with him out of spite. With Jiro completely defenseless in front of him, Amagi could have still tried to kill him and take him down with him, yet he chooses not to.

And that's what I liked most about his ending.

It's a shame that the fight itself couldn't leave me with a cool impression!

At the end of the episode we get the closing line from Jiro: "The mission's a go."

It definitely is a tease for a continuation! If we do get more of Black Torch, I'd genuinely like to see what it could become with a better execution of its action!!

Because I can see a GREAT DEAL of potential here.

I really can!

But potential only gets you so far. At some point, the actual show has to deliver on it, and that's where Black Torch disappointed me. Black Torch is an action-packed anime. The action is supposed to be one of its biggest selling points! And yet, somehow, there was a lot of action in it. They just weren't actioning LOL.

I know that sounds ridiculous, but I genuinely don't know how else to put it.

Let's just say that I wanted to come away from this series remembering the fights and the moments where the characters finally went all out.

Instead, I'm left thinking about all the action I wish the anime had actually shown me ༼ ◕ω◕ ༽

This anime is weird. It has the story and animation quality to easily earn an 8/10, yet the way it presents itself brings my rating down to just under 7.5/10. Still, I don't understand its low MAL rating. The art and animation are both quite good, the action scenes are exciting, and the story is unique, even if it draws inspiration from a mix of other anime and manga. The MC and supporting could be more complex, but despite that the MC is quite fun to watch thanks to his personality and behavior. Two things hold it back for me: 1. Sound design: The audio quality is weirdand inconsistent. Both the Japanese and original dubs occasionally sound as if they were recorded in an amateur studio. The music doesn't always fit the scenes and sometimes cuts off abruptly. It's not a major issue for me however.

2. Plot progression: It follows mainstream trends, yet the anime also seems to attempt something avant-garde—and doesn't quite pull it off. I've seen it wrongly compared to *Solo Leveling* simply because the MC looks somewhat similar and both series feature a system, but the MCs and their respective systems have little in common. The anime's attempt to balance mainstream appeal with more experimental storytelling results in an inconsistent flow and some unclear details (maybe just plot holes). The fight in the final episode, for example, was visually stunning and exciting, but how it was fought didn't make much sense (I am vague to avoid spoilers).

entry.title: Youkoso Jitsuryoku Shijou Shugi no Kyoushitsu e 4th Season: 2-nensei-hen 1 Gakki

results.review:
After four seasons, I'm honestly getting tired of Classroom of the Elite. Every season seems to follow the same formula: special exams, temporary alliances, attempts to expel students, and somehow, everything revolves around Ayanokoji. My biggest issue isn't that Ayanokoji is intelligent or powerful. It's that he rarely seems genuinely challenged. No matter how many people target him, he always comes out on top with barely any effort. At this point, the tension is almost nonexistent because I never believe he might actually lose. The supporting cast is another problem. So many characters have potential, yet their stories constantly circle back to Ayanokoji. I especially wish the femalecharacters had more independence instead of repeatedly becoming part of his romantic storyline.

That said, the season wasn't entirely disappointing. The White Room developments were interesting, and I enjoyed Ryuuen's confrontation with Hosen.

But the real highlight was Koenji. Watching him compete independently, outsmart his opponents, and ultimately win the island exam was genuinely satisfying. He's arrogant, but he actually backs up his confidence with results. I would love to see more focus on his character in future seasons.

Overall, Season 4 felt repetitive and predictable. Classroom of the Elite has an interesting premise and plenty of promising characters, but it keeps relying on the same formula to prove how exceptional Ayanokoji is.

I already know he's extraordinary. I just wish the story would give everyone else a chance to be interesting, too.

So glad Season 2 finally happened, really hoping the wait for a Season 3 won't take nearly as long. What makes this show great is how well it handles the military and political side of things. The character dynamics are solid, and Aoi Yuki’s voice acting for Tanya is phenomenal as always. The animation during the aerial combat scenes is also just fascinating to watch, and I really enjoyed the conflicting motivations of characters like Zettour and Mary Sue. The season definitely slowed down a bit in the middle, focusing heavily on political dialogue—whether to surrender, push forward with the war, or agree to peace talks. WhileI actually didn't mind the political depth, my biggest complaint this season is that the author feels a bit too hesitant to kill off named characters. Sure, Rudersdorf died, but that happened right at the very end. All of Tanya's core subordinates are still breathing, and major antagonists like Mary Sue are still around after all this time. Plus, I seriously doubt that Mikel guy is actually gone for good off-screen—he's definitely going to pop back up later.

Overall, I still really like the visuals, the core premise, and where the story is heading. I just hope future seasons bring back some real consequences and higher stakes to the war, especially since it's supposed to be a dark fantasy.

I have watched the 2014 korean "Liar Game" live action series and enjoyed it quite a bit. Of course I was happy to see the original manga getting finally an anime adaptation.... and got disappointed quite a lot. When watching the anime, I remembered most of the games in S1 and their outcomes already, so I focused instead on the characters and the differences. Since I don't remember every single detail of the live action, there were still some surprises left for me, as well as some new characters in the anime to enjoy. I don't know, why the live action worked so well for me atthe time, but when I watched the anime, it didn't feel right at all. Nao is still a very annoying character (I mean.. who is this naive??), although she makes some progress throughout S1. The games were still interesting, but their pacing felt off. Especially the smuggling game had too many episodes for my liking, that it got tedious to watch. The side characters are flat as wooden planks and follow basically the same pattern: Smug in the beginning, laughing maniacally in the middle, crying and begging in the end. 
It bothered me a lot, that nearly every opponent gets rescued, while Nao and Akiyama stay in the games. I get, why they are doing this, but it feels stiff and superficial to me. 

I really love shows like these normally. High stake games, psychological drama, intelligent characters exploiting rules and turn hopeless events around, etc. But somehow Liar Game didn't satisfy that. It had all the pieces, yet failed to place them to a full picture. I don't know, if the korean live action was actually that much better, since I don't remember everything after so long, but I remember, that it felt more tense and complete. I really wanted to love this adaptation and I wonder, if I would love it, if I hadn't seen the live action or if I would still miss some things. 
At this point, I'm unsure, if I want to watch S2, when it comes out.

Slice of Lowlife? Literal Gag Anime? Well, I personally didn't find it too gross but it comes down to your tolerances. If you are unaware, it has a lot of dirty humor that may or may not be a deal breaker for certain people. That said, the show has very high production value for what it is and it clearly comes from someone passionate. The show depicts lives of the residents of certain apartment complex ran by a good-natured landlord with beastfolk fetish. And the residents are mostly cat girls. Most of the characters rely on something to make their life more tolerable in one wayor another, for one reason or another: from substances to love dolls to streaming to "saving others". The line between melancholic reality and silly gags can sometimes be quite thin and the characters can be more relatable than one might expect or want.

As usual, voice work is really good and, as I've mentioned before, production value overall is on a level higher than you'd expect from a show like that.

All in all, it's a show that feels very genuine with likeable (pushing it in some cases though) failures and struggling victims of circumstances living life, finding solace in peers and vices or mingling with those supposedly outside of their intended social circles. And... All that said... I can't really recommend it to too many people because it is pretty polarizing.

entry.title: Tsuihou sareta Tensei Juukishi wa Game Chishiki de Musou suru

results.review:
What initially seemed like a fresh and unique animation style quickly revealed a much bigger problem: pacing. Despite being marketed as a standard 20-minute anime, a surprising amount of each episode is filled with content that adds little to the actual story progression. The recap and opening alone consume nearly five minutes, while the ending takes another two. That leaves roughly 13 minutes of episode content, but even that is stretched further with repeated animation sequences, recycled scenes, and frequent flashbacks. As a result, the amount of genuinely new material often feels closer to 10 minutes, sometimes even less. The excessive padding becomes increasingly noticeable over time.Rather than maintaining momentum, episodes regularly revisit previously shown content or reuse the same animation cuts, making the experience feel repetitive and artificially prolonged.

The story itself could likely be told far more effectively in 12 episodes. Instead, it feels as though enough unnecessary filler has been added to stretch the series to 26 episodes, resulting in slower pacing and a less engaging viewing experience overall.

I didn’t really understand the appeal of *Steins;Gate* that much. *Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood* is often called a masterpiece, but in my opinion, it doesn’t quite live up to that reputation. The art style is good, and the story has potential, but the execution isn’t as strong as I expected. There are several parts where I felt bored. I have similar issues with anime like *High School DxD*, *The Testament of Sister New Devil*, and *Hunter x Hunter*. Fans might consider these anime masterpieces, but from an average viewer’s perspective, they don’t necessarily deserve that label. That’s why I’d rate them somewhere between 7 and 8.5 ratherthan calling them masterpieces.
